title: "1.Load_data_from_googledrive"
format: html

## Overview

Our classification files from the Zooniverse get larger and larger (currently > 900 MB) which clogs both pushing to GitHub (due to large file size issue) and drive space.

Our current workflow involves parsing the JSON data in the zooniverse output in two steps: first, parse the `subject_data` column for the entire zooniverse file, and then subset the result by workflow to the iteratively parse the annotations data.

This code allows you to point to a file stored on google drive (either one that we downloaded directly from Zooniverse or another), subset it to the desired workflows, and do additional filtering so that you can write a smaller .csv file to use for analysis (or to keep in memory while you use the project but not write).

Using the scripts here requires the `googledrive` package.

## Set things up

```{r}
#| output: false
rm(list = ls())
library(tidyverse)
library(googledrive)
library(here)
```

## Get data from google drive
1.  Provide url to file on google drive (you must have at least "viewer" permission to see the file).

```{r}
file_id <- "https://drive.google.com/file/d/1QHKup4T7a9gZ0gCD8lK5Tx1xhkCMocYg/view?usp=sharing" #pulls zoo_subjects_through_Aug_2026.csv file

#need to pass the shared url for the correct csv file here
```

2.  Now get some info about the file. Requires `googledrive`

```{r}
my_file <- drive_get(file_id) #pulls info from google drive for the file
my_file$name 
#prints file name - check to make sure you have pulled correct file. But first will ask you to authenticate with google drive.
```

3.  Now read the file

```{r}
df <-read_csv(I(drive_read_string(my_file)))
#may be very slow!
```

## Subset to correct workflow and version

The Zooniverse uses different "workflows," each of which can have different versions (as they are tweaked), for classfying images.

We start by identifying the workflows present in our classification file

```{r}
unique(df$workflow_id)
unique(df$workflow_name)
```

The workflow we need to use is called "Species identification"

Let's filter just to that

```{r}
df <- df |> filter(workflow_name == "Species identification")
```

Now we need to see how many versions there are of that workflow

```{r}
unique(df$workflow_version)
```

Because the dataset has data from many different versions of this workflow, let's create a list that subsets the dataset by workflow version with each subset as a different element of the list.

```{r}
df_list <- list() #creates empty list}
df_list <- split(df, df$workflow_version) #creates list with each element a dataframe for a particular workflow version
```

Now if we look at that list of 15 different workflow versions, we can see that only 4 had significant amounts of data.

| Workflow version | Num rows |
|------------------|----------|
| 11.8             | 13033    |
| 29.1             | 73243    |
| 32.13            | 100516   |
| 34.14            | 37377    |

: Number of rows in specific workflows

All of the other versions of this main workflow have fewer than 20 rows.

Let's extract just these workflow versions.

```{r}
wf_versions <- c('11.8', '29.1','32.13', '34.14') #most recent workflows
```

Now subset the data to just those workflow versions:

```{r}
#now extract just the two workflow versions I need 
select_list <- df_list[wf_versions]

#if you want to just extract data directly into df and not list 
#df <- df |\> filter(workflow_version == 32.13 | workflow_version == 34.14) 
```

Now if you'd like to remove the larger datasets from the environment, run this code:

```{r}
rm(df)
rm(df_list)
```

This reduces us to a much smaller subset of the data in our environment.

Now write your list as an R data object so it can be imported into other code. Put it in `Data/PostZooniverse/Unflattened`

```{r}
write_rds(select_list, here("Data/PostZooniverse/Unflattened/Zoo_through_Aug_26_main_workflows.rds"))
```

Next, refer to the file called `2.Flatten_annotations_by_workflow` to see how we get the classification data from the file.

It assumes that you still have `df_list` and/or `select_list` in your workspace.If not, you can read in the list you just wrote.
